summary: The sample is a runnable Node.js app that meets the starter-prompt functionality: it seeds products (10k) and orders (20k), creates a DiskANN vector index (dimensions 1536), stores embeddings, exposes an Express UI, implements per-session memory persisted in a 'sessions' collection, and returns the top-5 recommendations with textual reasoning (OpenAI when available, deterministic synthetic fallback otherwise). Key runtime checks (seed, index creation, a one-shot vector search) were executed against the live cluster. Findings: the builder intentionally did not use LlamaIndex (no adapter/skill/SDK used), embeddings are generated from product text (not directly from co-purchase aggregates), some production-grade practices (retries honoring Retry-After, idempotent seed/upserts and unique indexes, infrastructure-as-code, documented clean-up steps, and explicit index/query tuning guidance) are missing or only partly implemented. Many best-practices are implemented and traceable to installed skills (singleton client, env-driven config, DiskANN index, normalized embeddings, $search/cosmosSearch usage).

requirement_results.requirement: Implement the app in Node.js and integrate LlamaIndex for vector search operations (code imports/uses Node.js and LlamaIndex).
requirement_results.evidence: app/package.json (dependencies) and src/* show Node.js usage; no LlamaIndex imports or usage found in src/*. Decision D004 (decisions.jsonl) records the explicit choice to implement an equivalent flow instead of LlamaIndex.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Provide a skill or packaged example for LlamaIndex Node bindings (e.g., add a 'llamaindex-node' skill and examples) or change the starter prompt to allow an equivalent agent implementation when LlamaIndex bindings are unavailable.

requirement_results.requirement: Use the Azure DocumentDB skill to read co-purchase order history from Azure DocumentDB (code shows an explicit call or adapter labeled "Azure DocumentDB skill" that queries the database).
requirement_results.evidence: The app queries the orders collection and computes co-purchase aggregates (app/src/server.js lines 149-158 and seed: orders inserted lines 152-165). However there is no adapter module explicitly named or labelled 'Azure DocumentDB skill'—the implementation uses the MongoDB driver directly. (events.jsonl shows documentdb-driver and other skills were loaded during the build, but the code does not present an adapter wrapper.)
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a thin adapter module (e.g., src/skill_adapters/documentdb.js) that wraps the DocumentDB skill guidance (or MCP calls) and update README to mention it; or update the skill to provide an explicit adapter template the builder can `require()`.

requirement_results.requirement: Parse order documents from Azure DocumentDB to extract co-purchase relationships (orders containing multiple product IDs) and use that history as the source data for generating product representations.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/server.js: aggregation over orders to compute co-purchase counts (lines 153-158). Seed creates orders with product arrays (app/src/seed.js lines 147-163).

requirement_results.requirement: Generate vector embeddings for products from the co-purchase data (code contains a clearly defined step that creates embeddings per product from the mined co-purchase information).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js generates embeddings for each product (lines 136-142) using a textual prompt `${title} - a sample item in category C${j % 20}` and getEmbeddingForText (lines 139-141). The code does not generate embeddings from aggregated co-purchase signals.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: In src/seed.js, compute a co-purchase summary or neighborhood for each product (e.g., top co-purchased product IDs or co-purchase counts) and pass that aggregated textual/numeric representation into getEmbeddingForText so embeddings reflect co-purchase relationships rather than only product title.

requirement_results.requirement: Persist those embeddings into a DiskANN index stored on disk (code builds and saves a DiskANN index file and uses it for subsequent lookups).
requirement_results.evidence: createVectorIndexIfNotExists in app/src/seed.js builds a cosmosSearch vector-diskann index (lines 79-116). events.jsonl shows createIndexes returned ok:1 and documentdb_list_indexes returned idx_embedding_diskann with cosmosSearchOptions { kind: 'vector-diskann', dimensions: 1536, similarity: 'COS' } (events.jsonl entries at timestamps around 02:25:21 and 02:26:20).

requirement_results.requirement: Build the agent using LlamaIndex so that vector search against the DiskANN index is performed via LlamaIndex APIs (code shows LlamaIndex creating/using the DiskANN-backed index for nearest-neighbor queries).
requirement_results.evidence: No LlamaIndex imports or use. The app uses direct MongoDB $search (cosmosSearch) aggregation pipelines (app/src/server.js lines 130-144) and a lightweight 'agent-like' flow; decision D004 records the deliberate choice to not use LlamaIndex.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either (a) include the LlamaIndex Node package and an example adapter that runs the LlamaIndex pipeline against the DiskANN-backed collection, or (b) add an explicit skill that documents how to wire LlamaIndex to Azure DocumentDB and provide a small adapter template in the agent kit.

requirement_results.requirement: Implement agent memory (explicitly named "agent memory") with per-session storage so recommendations are personalized across a user session and the memory influences returned recommendations (code demonstrates reading/writing session memory and using it when scoring or ranking items).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/server.js: session creation (createSession lines 37-42), recordViewedProduct (lines 47-50), getSessionMemory (lines 55-59), and session-based boost in scoring lines 162-169; the session is persisted in the 'sessions' collection and used in ranking.

requirement_results.requirement: Provide an interactive API or UI entry point that accepts a product ID and returns the top 5 recommended items plus a human-readable reasoning/explanation for each recommendation (response includes five product IDs/items and textual reasoning).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/server.js defines POST /api/recommend and returns top-5 recommendations plus explanation (lines 106-179). public/index.html posts productId to /api/recommend (lines 25-39).

requirement_results.requirement: Include a script in the repository that ingests exactly 20,000 product purchase transactions into Azure DocumentDB (the script inserts 20,000 order documents when run and the repository documents how to execute it).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.js sets NUM_ORDERS = 20000 and inserts orders in batched insertMany (lines 148-166). README documents npm run seed (app/README.md lines 21-24). events.jsonl shows seed completed and inserted the batches.

requirement_results.requirement: Use a configuration file for the Azure DocumentDB connection string and, when the connection string is missing or invalid, surface a clear, user-facing error message explaining the problem (code reads the connection string from a config file and explicitly validates it, failing with a clear error if absent or invalid).
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lists DOCUMENTDB_URI (lines 1-2). app/src/db.js checks process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI and exits with a clear error if missing (lines 16-21). README documents copying .env.example (app/README.md lines 21-24).

requirement_results.requirement: Provide an artistic, retailer-style UI for interacting with the agent (project contains frontend assets styled to look like an online retailer product page or catalog where users can submit a product ID and view recommendations).
requirement_results.evidence: public/index.html (Shoply branding, tag line) and public/style.css (styled hero and product area) create an artistic retailer-style UI (files app/public/index.html and app/public/style.css).

requirement_results.requirement: Add detailed comments before each method/function in the codebase (every function/method file contains a descriptive comment header explaining purpose, inputs, outputs, and high-level behavior to improve readability).
requirement_results.evidence: Files include descriptive headers and inline comments: app/src/db.js (file header and function comments lines 1-11 and 29-58), app/src/seed.js (lines 1-11 and function headers lines 23-56, 49-72, 75-116), app/src/server.js (file header and function headers lines 1-15, 34-42, 44-50, 52-59, 61-99).

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient instance (process-wide singleton) and tune connection-pool parameters for your deployment scenario rather than creating a new client per request.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js lines 26-41: getClient() implements a singleton client and reuses it.

checks.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters according to hosting: small maxPoolSize and short maxIdleTimeMS for serverless, larger pools (50+) and longer idle times for OLTP servers; set timeouts appropriate to expected latencies.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.js line 35 sets maxPoolSize: 10 but no other tuning (connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS/maxIdleTimeMS) and no config-driven tuning for hosting was implemented.
checks.fix: Expose and document pool/timeouts in config (e.g., read MAX_POOL_SIZE, CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS, SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS from env) and set defaults per hosting guidance (serverless vs OLTP).

checks.practice: The driver version is pinned and is one the service supports.
checks.evidence: app/package.json lists "mongodb": "^5.9.0" (app/package.json lines 14-20) and a package-lock.json is present. The project uses a caret range rather than an exact locked version in package.json, but package-lock.json provides a lockfile.
checks.searched: Searched agent kit and Node best-practice pages for a documented rule to require exact pinning in package.json
checks.fix: To be strict: pin exact driver version in package.json or include an explicit note in README that package-lock.json must be committed and used.
checks.what_would_help: A sentence in the driver or sample-kit README stating which driver minor/patch is tested and that package-lock.json must be committed.

checks.practice: Read the Azure DocumentDB connection string from an environment-backed config (.env or similar) at startup and fail fast with a clear error if it's missing.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example (line 2) and app/src/db.js lines 16-21 validate DOCUMENTDB_URI and exit with an explicit error message.

checks.practice: Always require TLS on connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: No code disables TLS; README and .env.example show TLS-aware example connection string. app/src/db.js uses the DOCUMENTDB_URI sourced from env, expecting the caller to provide TLS options in the URI (app/.env.example line 1 describes an example with ssl=true).

checks.practice: Create a vector index on your embedding field using the cosmosSearch operator, specifying the index kind (vector-diskann/vector-hnsw/vector-ivf), the embedding dimensions, and the similarity metric; the index's dimensions and similarity must match the embeddings you insert.
checks.evidence: app/src/seed.js builds createIndexes with cosmosSearchOptions.kind='vector-diskann', dimensions set to EMBEDDING_DIMS (lines 82-92, 99-111). events.jsonl shows createIndexes ok and documentdb_list_indexes returned idx_embedding_diskann with dimensions:1536.
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Prefer DiskANN for production-scale vector workloads on M30+ clusters and tune DiskANN build/query parameters (maxDegree, lBuild at index-build time; lSearch at query time) to trade recall vs latency.
checks.evidence: app/src/seed.js creates a DiskANN index but does not set or expose build-time parameters like lBuild or maxDegree, nor does the server exposure allow tuning query-time lSearch. (Index created with default DiskANN params, seed.js lines 86-92.)
checks.fix: Expose DiskANN build parameters in seed config (ENV vars) and expose lSearch in query code so users can tune recall/latency; document expected defaults for the sample size and how to change them.

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use the MCP or driver explain tools to verify vector-search plans and to project the searchScore (meta: 'searchScore') when you intend to re-rank results based on ANN scores.
checks.evidence: server.js projection includes score: { $meta: 'searchScore' } (app/src/server.js line 141) and later code uses r.score for scoring & re-ranking (lines 163-169). test_recommend.js also projects searchScore (app/src/test_recommend.js lines 25-26).
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use server-side aggregation pipelines ($match, $unwind, $group, $sort, $limit) to compute co-purchase counts and other aggregations rather than pulling large datasets to the client.
checks.evidence: server.js uses aggregation on orders to compute co-purchase counts (app/src/server.js lines 153-158). seed and queries are batched (seed.js uses insertMany lines 133-145 and 150-167).

checks.practice: Persist per-session memory in a dedicated sessions collection with a TTL index for ephemeral memory.
checks.evidence: The app persists sessions in the 'sessions' collection (app/src/server.js lines 37-41) and uses bounded viewed arrays via $push $slice (lines 47-50). However the seed/server does not create the TTL index automatically—no createIndex({createdAt:1},{expireAfterSeconds: ...}) step is present.
checks.fix: Create a TTL index in seed.js or document a manual step to create it (e.g., db.sessions.createIndex({createdAt:1},{expireAfterSeconds:3600})).

checks.practice: Use unique indexes to enforce uniqueness for primary keys used by the app (e.g., productId, sessionId) and use upserts carefully for idempotent seeding.
checks.evidence: seed.js inserts products and orders with insertMany (app/src/seed.js lines 133-145, 150-166) but seed does not create unique index on productId or upsert logic; a repeated run may create duplicates if insertMany doesn't rely on _id uniqueness or if the collection's unique index isn't set.
checks.fix: Create a unique index on {productId:1} (and sessionId if used) and either use upsert or check-existence logic in the seed so the script is idempotent (e.g., bulkWrite with upsert:true).

checks.practice: For large-scale ingestion prefer bulk-executor/SDK bulk APIs or distributed import tools and implement throughput-control, micro-batching, concurrency limits and retries to avoid sustained 429 throttling.
checks.evidence: seed.js batches inserts with batchSize = 500 and uses insertMany with ordered:false (app/src/seed.js lines 132-145, 150-166).
checks.source: Perform bulk operations on Azure Cosmos DB data

sources.title: Perform bulk operations on Azure Cosmos DB data

checks.practice: Store embedding metadata (model name, dims, embeddingVersion) with documents to detect mismatches and trigger re-embedding or index rebuilds when models change.
checks.evidence: Seed stores embedding arrays on products (app/src/seed.js line 141) but does not persist embedding model metadata (EMBEDDING_MODEL/EMBEDDING_DIMS) alongside each document.
checks.fix: Persist metadata fields such as embeddingModel and embeddingDims on each product document at ingest time (e.g., { productId, title, embedding, embeddingModel: EMBEDDING_MODEL, embeddingDims: EMBEDDING_DIMS }).

checks.practice: When ingesting embeddings at scale, validate vector dimensions match the index and reject or normalize inconsistent vectors before inserting to avoid silent search corruption.
checks.evidence: seed.js uses EMBEDDING_DIMS to shape synthetic embeddings (app/src/seed.js lines 20-21 and syntheticEmbedding lines 27-46), but does not validate that each produced embedding length matches EMBEDDING_DIMS before insert. There's no explicit per-document dims check.
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Add a pre-insert check in seed.js that validates embedding.length === EMBEDDING_DIMS and rejects or pads/truncates inconsistent vectors with an explicit log/error.

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Enable SDK retry semantics and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors and 429 responses, honoring Retry-After when present.
checks.evidence: No retry wrapper for DocumentDB operations, nor a wrapper for OpenAI calls; seed.js uses insertMany and logs warnings on batch failures but does not inspect 429/Retry-After or implement exponential backoff and retry.
checks.fix: Wrap network/DB calls in a retry helper that honors Retry-After and uses exponential backoff with jitter; for bulk ingest, throttle concurrency and implement retries for 429 responses.

checks.practice: Seed sizes and other hard choices should be recorded as a decision in decisions.jsonl for traceability (e.g., 10k products / 20k orders).
checks.evidence: app/src/seed.js uses NUM_PRODUCTS=10000 and NUM_ORDERS=20000 but there is no corresponding decision recorded in decisions.jsonl for those numeric choices.
checks.fix: Add a decision entry for seeding sizes (e.g., 'I chose 10k products and 20k orders for the sample to balance realism and run time').

decision_reviews.comment: D001 (approve build ready_with_gaps) is an operator-level action; events.jsonl records the readiness searches and build activity. The decision is consistent with the run and the subsequent build steps.

D002 chose the official mongodb npm driver and a singleton client. Code (app/src/db.js) implements a singleton and package.json depends on mongodb ^5.9.0. events.jsonl shows the documentdb-driver skill was loaded.

D003 (OpenAI with deterministic fallback) is reflected in code: seed.js getEmbeddingForText returns syntheticEmbedding when OPENAI_API_KEY is missing (app/src/seed.js lines 53-56). The build log and README also describe the fallback.

D004 (implementing a lightweight agent flow instead of LlamaIndex) is supported by the event trace: no LlamaIndex skill or package was loaded, and the code implements an equivalent pipeline. The reason (uncertain LlamaIndex Node availability) is documented in readiness findings.

D005 (persist session memory in DocumentDB sessions collection) was implemented (app/src/server.js). The decision's reason_source is 'model_default' (decisions.jsonl) rather than anchored in a skill or operator instruction. It's a reasonable choice but originated from model default behavior; the run trace does not show a skill prescribing sessions. Consider documenting why DocumentDB (sessions collection) was chosen vs Redis/in-memory in README.

D006 chose DiskANN and dimensions 1536. The index was created and verified (events.jsonl includes createIndexes ok and documentdb_list_indexes shows idx_embedding_diskann with dimensions 1536). The DocumentDB vector-search skills were loaded.

D007 removed node-fetch after npm install failed; events.jsonl shows npm install error for node-fetch then an updated package.json and a successful npm install. The decision is traceable in the events log.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public, discoverable guidance or agent-kit skill shows how to integrate LlamaIndex Node bindings with Azure DocumentDB's vector store (DiskANN) or provides a copy-paste adapter template.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Agent kit skills, Microsoft Learn vector-search docs, and run-time readiness notes (events.jsonl searches for LlamaIndex/Node bindings).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder chose not to use LlamaIndex and implemented an equivalent lightweight agent pipeline. This means the published sample does not demonstrate LlamaIndex usage the starter prompt requested.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a skill 'llamaindex-node' to the agent kit with: (1) a minimal example that constructs a LlamaIndex index over DocumentDB's DiskANN-backed collection; (2) an adapter module that shows how to translate LlamaIndex semantics into cosmosSearch queries (createIndexes + $search) and how to persist metadata; (3) a note on required npm package names/versions and an example package.json.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A small copy-paste 'createIndexes' runCommand example with recommended DiskANN parameters for a sample-size catalog (10k) and a short explanation of recommended lBuild/lSearch values and their effect.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill and Microsoft Learn vector-search docs; the guidance exists but a ready-to-copy snippet for sample authors was not included in the local sample kit docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample created a DiskANN index with defaults; runtime behaved, but authors and readers may not know which params to change for larger datasets.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short page named 'Sample: create DiskANN index for product catalog' containing the createIndexes runCommand JSON for DiskANN and suggested defaults for NUM_PRODUCTS=10k (e.g., lBuild=40, maxDegree=64) and recommended query-time lSearch values for k=10. Include a note on expected build time and memory.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Explicit examples mapping popular embedding models to index 'dimensions' and a recommended env var name convention for embedding model/dim pairs.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill, Microsoft Learn vector docs, readiness notes.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder assumed text-embedding-3-small → 1536 dims; the run succeeded. Without explicit guidance, other authors may pick mismatched dims and silently corrupt nearest-neighbour behavior.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A brief table in the vector-search quickstart: 'Model name → default dims' (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small:1536, text-embedding-3-large:3072, etc.), and a note: 'Store embeddingModel and embeddingDims with each document; validate dims on ingest.'

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A concrete example (code snippet) that creates a TTL index on the sessions collection (e.g., db.sessions.createIndex({ createdAt:1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 3600 })).
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-indexing skill and sample repo; skill documents TTL semantics but sample lacked the createIndex snippet.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Sessions are persisted but there is no automatic expiry defined; long-term run could accumulate session documents.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'create session TTL index' snippet in seed.js (or README) that shows createIndex with expireAfterSeconds and explains the Date field requirement.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A ready-to-use retry helper that honours Retry-After and applies exponential backoff/jitter for DocumentDB SDK calls and external embedding/LLM calls.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Throttling docs and documentdb-query-optimizer and connection skills; no packaged helper shipped in the agent kit for Node.js sample authors.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Seed script uses batched insertMany but does not implement retries for 429s, increasing the risk of failed or partial ingestion under throttling.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Ship a small Node.js helper (retryWithBackoff) as part of the agent-kit or sample template showing how to inspect HTTP 429/Retry-After and how to backoff and retry DB and HTTP calls.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A recommended pattern and a code snippet that: create unique indexes on productId, use bulkWrite upserts for idempotent seeds, and document how to re-run the seed safely.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-indexing skill and agent-kit samples; guidance present in pieces but not a one-shot snippet in the kit.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The seed works but is not idempotent; repeated runs may create duplicates if unique indexes are not present or upsert not used.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add an 'idempotent seed' section to the seed example showing createIndex({productId:1},{unique:true}) and using bulkWrite with upsert:true to avoid duplicates.

doc_gaps.topic: Guidance for using deterministic synthetic embeddings in tests
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Public guidance that explicitly recommends deterministic synthetic embeddings for CI and local dev when external embedding APIs are unavailable.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Searches for 'deterministic synthetic embeddings' returned no authoritative guidance (discovered_practices shows this as prior_knowledge_only).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder implemented deterministic synthetic embeddings (good), but this is a prior-knowledge pattern that is not documented for Azure DocumentDB authors; agents may not automatically adopt the pattern.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short dev/testing guidance page: 'Testing vector apps without external APIs' that covers deterministic embeddings, seeding, and env flags to avoid external calls.
